SECTION: 2. Coverage Grant - Sudden And Accidental Discharge

2. COVERAGE GRANT - SUDDEN AND ACCIDENTAL DISCHARGE
2.1 We cover direct physical loss to covered property caused by the sudden and accidental discharge, leakage or overflow of water or steam from a plumbing, heating, air conditioning, fire protective sprinkler system, or household appliance located within the described dwelling. A supply line that ruptures, splits or otherwise fails abruptly is a sudden and accidental discharge for the purposes of this clause, and loss resulting from it is covered subject to the exclusions in Clause 3 and the limits in Clause 5.

structure.answer: No. Exclusion E‑17 only covers “constant or repeated seepage or leakage … over a period of fourteen (14) days or more” and “does NOT apply to a sudden and accidental discharge” [chunk_id=HO-0304_water_damage_ed_03-24.pdf#41a175ccd467f366 | HO-0304 (edition 03‑24) | Exclusion Table 3.1]. Because a ruptured supply line is an abrupt failure that is a “sudden and accidental discharge” under Clause 2.1, E‑17 is not triggered even though the leak was not discovered for twenty days [chunk_id=HO-0304_water_damage_ed_03-24.pdf#ad1f3ac26ec308ef | HO-0304 (edition 03‑24) | Exclusion Table 3.1].

recursive.answer: Yes. Because the water escaped for twenty days—more than the fourteen‑day period that distinguishes seepage from a sudden, accidental discharge—the loss is classified as seepage and is excluded absolutely under exclusion E‑17 of HO‑0304. The exclusion states that “Constant or repeated seepage or leakage of water occurring over a period of fourteen (14) days or more… Disposition: Excluded absolutely; does NOT apply to a sudden and accidental discharge under Clause 2.1” [chunk_id=HO-0304_water_damage_ed_03-24.pdf#932862290fd27d45 | HO-0304 (edition 03‑24) | E‑17] and the definition of seepage notes that a process lasting fourteen days or more is adjudicated as seepage, not a sudden accidental event [chunk_id=HO-0710_definitions_general_conditions_ed_11-23.pdf#ee8c04643e625807 | HO-0710 (edition 11‑23) | Clause 2.2]. The note in the same form further confirms that E‑17 is directed at a slow, ongoing failure and is not triggered by an abrupt rupture lasting less than fourteen days [chunk_id=HO-0304_water_damage_ed_03-24.pdf#61063947ac023d64 | HO-0304 (edition 03‑24) | 4. Conditions Precedent To Payment].

SECTION: 2. Definitions

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Sudden and accidental means an event which is both abrupt in onset and unintended by the insured, and which occurs at an identifiable point in time. An event is not sudden and accidental merely because its consequences were unexpected. A process which develops gradually over a period of fourteen (14) days or more is not sudden and accidental however unintended its result, and is adjudicated as seepage.
2.2 Supply line means any pipe, hose, tube, fitting or connector which conveys water under mains pressure to a fixture, appliance or system within the described dwelling, up to and including the shut-off valve serving that fixture, appliance or system. A supply line does not include a waste, soil or drainage pipe, which is a drain line.

structure.answer: Yes. Exclusion E‑17 covers “constant or repeated seepage or leakage of water occurring over a period of fourteen (14) days or more…[and] does NOT apply to a sudden and accidental discharge” [chunk_id=HO-0304_water_damage_ed_03-24.pdf#41a175ccd467f366 | HO-0304 | Exclusion Table 3.1]. Because the water seeped for twenty days, the loss meets the “over a period of fourteen days or more” trigger. The definition of “sudden and accidental” states that a process that develops gradually over fourteen days or more is not sudden and accidental but is adjudicated as seepage [chunk_id=HO-0710_definitions_general_conditions_ed_11-23.pdf#4a3af5524b7032d0 | HO-0710 | 2.1]. Thus the situation is excluded under E‑17. (See also the note that E‑17 is directed at a slow, ongoing failure and is not triggered by an abrupt rupture) [chunk_id=HO-0304_water_damage_ed_03-24.pdf#ad1f3ac26ec308ef | HO-0304 | Exclusion Table 3.1].
